name: Chad
summary_text: Chad is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct criminalised since 2017 (misdemeanour, up to 2 years); junta-adjacent governance; no LGR; no community infrastructure; very thin data.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Chad: documents the legal status — same-sex conduct criminalised under the 2017 penal code.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Chad-specific page); the Trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people, which include Chad.

sources.title: Chad - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Chad: official assessment - the 2017 Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct; significant societal stigma; no prosecutions reported.
US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Chad (archived): pre-criminalisation baseline - no law against homosexuality at the time; general human-rights context.
US State Department 2006 Human Rights Report for Chad: documents the Deby regime's abuses - extrajudicial killings, torture, MINURCAT withdrawal - general context.

sources.title: Anti-LGBT Groups Making Inroads Across East Africa | HuffPost The World Post
sources.claim_summary: HuffPost/GroundTruth Project (June 2015): 'Anti-LGBT Groups Making Inroads Across East Africa' - while further criminalisation failed in Ethiopia and Rwanda, it succeeded in Chad and Nigeria - US evangelical influence on African anti-gay laws.
